# Independent audit: critical nonheavy 3+2 folded-Ball obstruction


`candidate fc66a0bec6505bfb`.
Result: **PASS after one boundary wording correction**, now applied.

## Actual source and buffer geometry

The rectangle directions u,v are orthonormal. Its area is exactly
4(3/10)(109/270)=109/225, and its inscribed radius is3/10.
Its coordinate minimum is 2/3-19/(27 sqrt(2))>0. The maximum
coordinate sum of A+R is 1/5+4/3+(3/10)sqrt(2)<2. Both strict
inequalities follow from the displayed positive-square comparisons.
They prove (A+R)/2 subset int T, so the actual middle fiber is T,
the endpoint sections are A,R, and the complete base is {-1,0,1}.
The full-dimensional body and all three positive full-dimensional
fibers are real; no convexification enlargement is omitted.

The total mass is452/450=226/225. The three individual masses are
9/450,225/450,218/450, all strictly below226/450. Thus the strict
nonheavy premise is verified exactly, including the largest fiber.

Both buffer rectangles lie in the radius3/10 ball: their extreme
squared radii are9/100 and221/2500<9/100. Their interiors are
disjoint and their common boundary segment has zero area, giving
exact total area14/625>1/50. The source originally called the
closed rectangles disjoint; the author corrected this to disjoint
interiors during the audit. No numerical estimate of a circular
cap is required and no mass is lost at the shared boundary.

## Every ambient halfspace and the five critical caps

For a unit continuous direction, failure to contain every point of
A gives an actual point a_0 with margin below zero. The resulting
right-center margin is strictly greater than w dot a_0>=-1/5.
Therefore the full fixed-height ball cap from the buffer calculation
is contained in the right trace. Together with the middle centroid
Grunbaum contribution2/9 this is strictly more than Q. If A is
fully contained, it directly contributes the required1/50. Purely
integer containing caps retain the entire middle fiber and exceed
Q. This proves the complete lower bound at (0,g), not merely one
for the displayed normal directions.

At (1,2g), the own centrally symmetric R fiber supplies Q against
every nonvertical containing halfspace and its full area against
purely integer halfspaces. Thus both claimed contacts have depth
at least Q. The three isolated canonical middle caps each contribute
1/50+2/9=Q, capture all of A, and strictly miss R. Their summed
margin is -30z and hence they cover every plane over z<=0.
The isolated opposite pair at the right contact strictly misses
A,T and bisects R, also with mass Q. It covers every plane over
z>=1. No integer base lies between these two half-lines.

This five-cap cover bounds the depth at EVERY actual source point
above by Q. Both lower-bound points are therefore genuinely globally
deepest and every displayed cap is critical. The positive continuous
normal ranks are two and one as claimed. Closed supporting traces
and purely integer boundary mass are accounted for in their proper
branches.

## Shear, fold, and exact nonconvexity

The map x->x-(z+1)g is a single fiber shear of Jacobian one taking
both contacts to continuous zero. The left fiber stays A, the middle
becomes T-g, and the right becomes centered at zero. Folding the
left fiber by factor1/2 requires area density4; thus the displayed
ordinary density retains exactly its original mass1/50. It is not
mistaken for uniform area or for a lattice-preserving projective
map. Its added triangle lies in the middle triangle.

Each q_i lies on the original facet x_1+x_2=1/3. Along q_1 and
q_2 the negative second coordinate excludes the added triangle
except at the origin, and the middle triangular radial endpoint
is exactly parameter1. Their gauges are both1. Along q_3 the small
triangle persists exactly to parameter3/10. Consequently the full
radial integral is1+4(3/10)^2=34/25 and the gauge is5/sqrt(34)<1.
The exact midpoint relation then violates gauge convexity strictly.

The radial star body contains the original convex triangle with
zero in its interior, so its gauge is well-defined and positive in
every nonzero direction. If that body were convex, its Minkowski
gauge would be convex. The displayed inequality is therefore an
actual nonconvexity certificate. It does not arise from altered
values on a null radial boundary: the unaffected rays stay strictly
outside the added triangle's angular cone and the affected ray is
strictly within it.

## Scope

The normalized maximum is109/452, above2/9 by77/4068. Thus the
example refutes automatic convexity of this specified one-sided
sampled fold even under actual compatibility, two deepest contacts,
a genuinely critical3+2 cover, and strict nonheavy fibers. It does
not refute the separately proved slab-erosion theorem, which never
assumes this fold convexity, or any transfer claim requiring a
further below-target hypothesis. It is not an OC counterexample.
